diagnosis.summary: The executor timed out after 35 minutes while still in the package-installation phase on all four nodes; no evidence in the sampled log shows Galera configuration (my.cnf/wsrep settings), cluster bootstrap, or node4 join ever being attempted. The two clearly observed problems are (1) severe apt/network flakiness against Ubuntu mirrors that forced repeated multi-minute retries and consumed most of the time budget, and (2) after mariadb-server-10.0 finally installed on node1, systemd reported the mariadb.service unit as 'not-found', meaning the expected service name did not exist post-install.

evidence.finding: Before any install, mysql/mariadb binaries did not exist and mariadb.service was inactive on all four nodes (fresh Ubuntu 16.04 Xenial i386 images, no DB packaged pre-installed).
All four 'apt-get update' invocations hit the 120s proxy read timeout and were recorded as failed, indicating slow/unreliable outbound network or mirror responsiveness from the start.

evidence.source: install.log tails across multiple polling execs (node1-4, ~01:43-01:57)
evidence.finding: apt-get install for mariadb-server-10.0/galera-3/rsync repeatedly hit 'Connection failed' errors against archive.ubuntu.com and security.ubuntu.com mirrors (e.g. IP 91.189.92.24, 91.189.91.82), requiring multiple sleep/retry poll cycles per node; total install time stretched past 15+ minutes per node.

All nodes are Ubuntu 16.04.7 LTS (Xenial) on i386 (32-bit) architecture, an unusual choice that narrows available mirror package versions and may correlate with the connection failures/slowness (i386 xenial packages are lower-traffic/lower-priority mirror paths).

'dpkg -l' confirms mariadb-server-10.0 10.0.38-0ubuntu0.16.04.1 installed, but 'systemctl status mariadb' reports 'Loaded: not-found (Reason: No such file or directory)' and 'Active: inactive (dead)' — the mariadb.service unit does not exist under that name on this package/OS combination.

111 total command records with only 55 terminal (33 of those omitted from the sample) and 56 requested-only (never completed) — the sampled window ends during node1's post-install service check, with no later records showing my.cnf edits, wsrep_cluster_address configuration, galera bootstrap, or any node4-specific join steps. Evidence is insufficient to say whether those steps were attempted later in the run before the timeout.

likely_causes.cause: Primary/root cause: the run exhausted its 2100s budget almost entirely on apt-get update/install across 4 nodes due to unreliable/slow connectivity to Ubuntu package mirrors, leaving little or no time for actual Galera configuration and node4 join.

Secondary issue: on this Ubuntu 16.04 mariadb-server-10.0 package, the running service is registered under a different unit name (commonly 'mysql.service', not 'mariadb.service' on Xenial) — the executor's readiness checks used 'systemctl is-active mariadb', which would report inactive/not-found even if the DB were actually starting correctly, likely causing unnecessary further debugging/retry loops.

The i386 (32-bit) node architecture may have contributed to mirror/package-availability slowness or failures, since i386 xenial-security/xenial-updates paths are lower-traffic and more prone to transient 'Connection failed' errors than amd64.

No evidence in the sample that /etc/hosts population via CLUSTER_HOSTS or SSH keypair setup ever completed cleanly, since those commands were bundled with the failing apt-get update call and its failure state for that combined command is ambiguous (the 'tee' part may have succeeded even though the whole line was marked failed due to apt-get timeout).

next_attempt_guidance: On the fresh cluster, first verify basic network reachability and mirror latency with lightweight commands (e.g. a single small apt-get update with a short explicit timeout, or curl -sI to the mirror) before committing to the full package install command, so mirror flakiness is caught early and cheaply rather than through repeated 120s-timeout retries.

Split 'echo CLUSTER_HOSTS >> /etc/hosts' and 'apt-get update' into separate exec calls (per platform guidance: one logical step per exec) so a mirror timeout on update doesn't leave ambiguous state about whether /etc/hosts was written.

Do not use 'systemctl is-active mariadb' as the sole readiness check on Ubuntu 16.04/mariadb-server-10.0; also check 'systemctl is-active mysql' and 'service mysql status', since the unit may be registered under the legacy 'mysql' name on this OS/package combination — confirm the actual unit name via 'systemctl list-units | grep -i -E "mysql|mariadb"' before concluding the service is missing.

Budget time explicitly: given ~15+ minutes per node for install alone in the prior attempt, either run installs on all 4 nodes in parallel (background + poll per the platform's streaming pattern) rather than sequentially, or request a longer time allowance, so there is time left for wsrep_cluster_address configuration, bootstrap of the first node, sequential join of node2/node3, and finally adding node4 with its own galera config and SST.

If apt package installation continues to be unreliable due to mirror connectivity, consider checking whether a regional/local mirror or apt proxy is expected in this environment, since 'Connection failed' errors against archive.ubuntu.com/security.ubuntu.com were the dominant failure mode and are an environment/network characteristic, not a Galera configuration issue.

Confirm the node's architecture (i386 vs amd64) up front; if i386 was unintended, flag it, since it constrains which mirror paths and package versions are available and may be the source of the observed connection instability.

When finally configuring Galera, apply the my.cnf wsrep_cluster_address and wsrep_node_address settings consistently across all 4 nodes from the start (including node4) rather than treating node4 as an afterthought, and plan for an SST (e.g. rsync-based, since 'rsync' was already installed) to populate node4 from an existing member's data.
